questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The warm climate, the city, the study environment. I checked online for the courses that were available, and I found that they lined up well with what I wanted.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a bit confusion initially due to covid as to whether the classes were going to be held online or in person. But we got a mail send with the information and how to enroll. The information that was available online concerning housing and so on was fine, although most were in spanish or catalan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to the international office when I arrived and they provided me with the steps on how to enroll. I had to change some courses so the process took a bit longer than it should have.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Housing can be a bit difficult to find. I stayed at a hostel for the first couple weeks until I found something.I initially wanted to sublet, but it is not really a thing here. There are some firms that specialize in student accomadation, but it is really expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great, but some places can be really touristy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After you have signed your learning agreement etc. you go to the international office where they enroll you oficially, so you can enter the online campus site and have access to your courses there. I found it a bit confusing as to the rules on what classes you could take, but I think I was also a special case, as the course i was enrolled in had classes provided by different universities. I had to change my classes, so the final registration took some time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can communicate by mail and otherwise you can go to the international office where they can help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not so succesful initially, as there were some that overlapped schedule-wise, and some that were provided by other universities. But I ended up finding some classes I really liked, though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you enroll in the CCiL course, be sure that you are allowed to take the classes (as it is interdiciplary and covered by multiple universities), and thouroughly check the schedules for classes online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It varied a lot. As the course was interdiciplinary (philosophy, psychology, linguistics), some classes had to provide some introductionary material to the subjects we were covering. Others I found to be pretty specialized in one field, so there were more expectations on sudent knowledge. Overall, I think the classes and teachers struck a fine balance.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much the same, were students are expected to intervene with questions. For some classes, the first half were devoted to a presentation of the subject while the second part were more open to discussion. Other classes had more of a "teacher teaches" style.  I think one difference may be that UCPH is more keen on 'activating the students', where some time in class is devoted to group work or small discussions with your side partner. That was not really a thing here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: The Nature of language, Action, perception and consciuosness, Developing language and cognition, Interdisciplary application of linguistics, Language and cognition.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It really depends on what you what and how much work you want to put in. For me, as a philosophy student, I actually found the psychology classes I took to be really interesting and with much up-to-date science and experiments, although I had to familirize myself with a lot of concepts and methods that I had not really been introduced to before.  (Action, perception and consciuosness, Developing language and cognition) 'Interdisciplinary application of linguistics' provided a very good introduction to some topics in biolinguistics, and the teacher was very open to discuss and present topics the students wanted covered.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: As I had to stay in a hostel the first couple weeks, that made food and and accomodation a bit more expensive than I expected. I also lost my wallet the first week, so that was also problematic.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Generally I think I expected things to be more expensive. Food and groceries (and eggs especially) are pretty cheap, although some specific products (some dairy, fish) can be more expensive than in Denmark. Going and eating out is also pretty cheap, so overall I would say the prices are around 75 % of what they are in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didnt participate much in activities that were offered by the university, but I guess they host some debates and other social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going on hikes in the nature sorrounding Barcelona. Going to some of the small seasite towns. Or just going to the beach in the afternoon.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visiting some of the nearby towns - like Sitges or Tarragona - is a great day experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy - it is more easygoing than Denmark. The hardest thing is the eating schedules.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are some Whatsapp groups where a lot of activities is hosted. Also just going to the library or hanging around Campus you will generally meet people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are generally very nice and easy to chat with. The weather is great and the culture is very outgoing. You can go to a cafe at all times of the day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Be sure that you have the relevant information regarding registering courses and availability - preferably before you leave.  2. Make sure to be part of the Whatsapp groups - a lot of great activities are posted there. 3. For housing - a site like Idealista is great, but make sure you don't get caught with some of the very expensive options offered by housing firms.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Generally, communicating in english is fine, but some information is only available in spanish or catalan - so there can be a language mixup sometimes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and exploring some subjects I hadn't touched before.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
